analysis:
To ensure that every face of the 3x3x3 cube contains at least one marked point, we need to consider the structure of the cube. A 3x3x3 cube has 6 faces, each of which is a 3x3 grid. We need to place points in such a way that no face is left without a marked point.

One effective strategy is to place points at the centers of the faces. Since there are 6 faces, placing a point at the center of each face will ensure that every face has at least one marked point. This configuration uses exactly 6 points.

To verify that 6 points are indeed the minimum, consider that if we use fewer than 6 points, at least one face will not have a marked point. For example, if we use only 5 points, at least one face will be missing a point because there are 6 faces and only 5 points available.

Therefore, the minimum number of points that must be marked on a 3x3x3 cube such that every face of the cube contains at least one marked point is 6.
